label: context.reference
description: Find, read, activate and publish scoped knowledge and capability selections.
text:
Reusable knowledge and capability selections live in ordinary artifacts. A bound context.collection exposes its entries through context.discover and context.read. Descriptions help you choose entries; they grant no role or authority.

Use a supplied catalogue to notice relevant knowledge. It pins sources and revisions, may cover only one page, and may predate corrections. Before substantial work, discover relevant readable collections if the catalogue is absent, incomplete or needs refreshing. A trivial, self-contained task needs no unrelated scan. context.discover with no arguments lists sources. Query or page a relevant source, follow its cursor, and read an entry using the returned source, entry_id and revision. Queries are literal filters; no word match does not prove a capability is absent. Rediscover stale revisions rather than guessing ids or replacing context in accepted work.

Reading an entry does not activate its references or grant tools, credentials, rooms or routes. External artifact bodies need their own bindings. Request the publication's exact selection through declared run creation or current-run amendment, inspect the preview and effect receipt, and check the target's formed grant. Its worker ceiling and EE policy decide authority. Use granted file tools to author missing descriptors or delegate through an allowed interface. A worker/provider/template entry can guide a new run; it cannot replace the provider of an accepted turn.

Publish useful durable knowledge, procedures, corrections and working capabilities to a writable collection for the intended audience. Put the useful conclusion and applicability in a short description; keep detailed steps, configuration and evidence in content. Preserve the original scope, evidence refs, assumptions and freshness limits. Base user preferences on the user's statements, keeping inference distinct. Never save secrets, sensitive descriptions or whole transcripts. Use a separately bound collection for private project knowledge.

context.prepare_publication plans a write without applying it. Supply source, a complete entry and expected_revision (null only for a new id). Inspect the returned file.write arguments and execute them through the granted writer. Its successful receipt proves publication. After an uncertain write, inspect the receipt and current entry before retrying. Published entries are discoverable by other tasks bound to the collection.

Entry fields: schema_version 1, source-local id, title, description, applicability, state (active or withdrawn), scope, optional content, selection and optional requires. content holds text and evidence refs. selection uses context_artifact_bindings, payload_artifact_bindings, selected_tools, selected_worker_environment_kinds, door_host_slots, external_inputs, external_relays and model_outputs; omitted lists are empty. Keep exact descriptor ids and state missing prerequisites. scope may restrict ee_ids or worker_interfaces; omitted restrictions add no privacy beyond the collection binding. A run-private worker pin is unsuitable for knowledge intended for independent future runs; use the intended EE scope or a separate collection. Build and validate the owner/package/descriptors before advertising executable selections.

Update an entry using its observed revision. Withdraw stale guidance with state withdrawn, preserving earlier evidence. Later discovery sees the update; accepted results retain the version they used. Consolidation uses these same tools, in this run or another run reached through an explicit interface.
